description.en: Dive into multi-head self-attention — the core operation of Transformers — and understand how Q, K, V projections enable each token to attend to every other token.

story_variants.en:
## Self-Attention: Q, K, V Matrices

In **self-attention**, the queries, keys, and values all come from the **same sequence**. Every token attends to every other token — letting the model capture long-range dependencies in a single operation.

### Projecting to Q, K, V

Given input embeddings `X` (shape: [seq_len, d_model]), we create Q, K, V by linear projections:

```python
W_Q = np.random.randn(d_model, d_k)  # (512, 64)
W_K = np.random.randn(d_model, d_k)  # (512, 64)
W_V = np.random.randn(d_model, d_v)  # (512, 64)

Q = X @ W_Q   # (seq_len, d_k)
K = X @ W_K   # (seq_len, d_k)
V = X @ W_V   # (seq_len, d_v)
```

### Multi-Head Attention

Instead of one set of Q/K/V, use **h heads** in parallel — each head can attend to different relationships:

```
head_i = Attention(Q·W_Qi, K·W_Ki, V·W_Vi)
MultiHead = Concat(head_1, ..., head_h) · W_O
```

| GPT-2 Small | Value |
|------------|-------|
| d_model | 768 |
| n_heads | 12 |
| d_k per head | 64 |
| n_layers | 12 |

### Attention Mask

For **causal** (decoder) self-attention, we mask future positions so the model cannot look ahead:

```python
mask = np.tril(np.ones((seq_len, seq_len)))  # lower triangle
scores = scores * mask + (1 - mask) * (-1e9) # set upper to -inf
weights = softmax(scores)  # masked positions get weight ≈ 0
```

### Positional Encoding

> **Key Concept:** Self-attention has no notion of position — the same output regardless of word order. **Positional encodings** are added to input embeddings to inject order information. Transformers use sine/cosine waves at different frequencies.

```python
PE[pos, 2i]   = sin(pos / 10000^(2i/d_model))
PE[pos, 2i+1] = cos(pos / 10000^(2i/d_model))
```

steps.line: Q = X @ W_Q  # project to query space

explanation.en: Each row asks: 'what am I looking for?'

steps.line: K = X @ W_K  # project to key space

explanation.en: Each row says: 'I contain this information'

steps.line: V = X @ W_V  # project to value space

explanation.en: Each row says: 'here is my content'
Every token compares with every other token: O(n²) complexity
Weighted blend of all value vectors

animation_sequence.code:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn

# Multi-Head Self-Attention
mha = nn.MultiheadAttention(embed_dim=64, num_heads=8, batch_first=True)
x = torch.randn(2, 10, 64)  # batch=2, seq=10, dim=64

# Self-attention: Q=K=V=x
attn_output, attn_weights = mha(x, x, x)
print(f'Input: {x.shape}')
print(f'Output: {attn_output.shape}')
print(f'Attention weights: {attn_weights.shape}')

instruction.en: Implement `causal_mask(seq_len)` that returns a lower-triangular boolean matrix of shape `(seq_len, seq_len)`. Positions where mask is False should be set to -1e9 in the attention scores (not attended to).

hints.en: Use np.tril(np.ones((n, n), dtype=bool)) for the lower triangle
Position (i,j) should be True if j <= i (can see current and past tokens)
For a 4-token sequence: row 0 sees only token 0, row 3 sees tokens 0-3

q.en: In self-attention, where do the queries, keys and values come from?
q.ta: self-attention-இல் queries, keys, values எங்கிருந்து வருகின்றன?

en: All three come from the same input sequence
Queries from the input, keys and values from the encoder
Q, K, V are fixed random matrices, not tied to the input
ta: Queries உள்ளீட்டிலிருந்து, keys மற்றும் values encoder-இலிருந்து
Q, K, V உள்ளீட்டுடன் தொடர்பில்லாத நிலையான random அணிகள்

q.en: X has shape (10, 512) and W_Q has shape (512, 64). What is the shape of Q = X @ W_Q?
q.ta: X-இன் வடிவம் (10, 512), W_Q-இன் வடிவம் (512, 64). Q = X @ W_Q-இன் வடிவம் என்ன?

q.en: A causal mask is written as mask = np.triu(np.ones((n, n), dtype=bool)). What is the mistake?
q.ta: ஒரு causal mask இவ்வாறு எழுதப்பட்டது: mask = np.triu(np.ones((n, n), dtype=bool)). இதில் உள்ள பிழை என்ன?

en: dtype=bool is not allowed with np.ones
The shape should be (n, n+1) to include the current token
triu keeps the upper triangle, so tokens see future positions
No mistake: triu and tril give the same causal mask
ta: தற்போதைய token-ஐ சேர்க்க வடிவம் (n, n+1) ஆக இருக்க வேண்டும்
triu மேல் முக்கோணத்தை வைக்கிறது, அதனால் tokens எதிர்கால நிலைகளைப் பார்க்கும்
பிழை இல்லை: triu, tril இரண்டும் ஒரே causal mask தரும்

under_the_hood.summary: Self-attention multiplies the token matrix X by three learned matrices to get Q, K and V, scores every pair of tokens with QKᵀ / sqrt(d_k), applies softmax row by row, and multiplies by V; multiple heads do this in parallel on smaller slices.

steps.title: Project X into Q, K and V
steps.body: X holds one row per token, shape (seq_len, d_model). Q = X W_Q, K = X W_K, V = X W_V, each with its own learned matrix, for example 512 x 64 per head. The same token gets three different roles: what it looks for, what it offers to be found by, and what it passes on.

steps.title: Score every pair at once
steps.body: Toy example with 3 tokens and d_k = 2: let Q = K = [[1, 0], [0, 1], [1, 1]]. QKᵀ is a 3 x 3 matrix of all dot products: [[1, 0, 1], [0, 1, 1], [1, 1, 2]]. Row i holds token i's score against every token, itself included. Dividing by sqrt(2) keeps the values moderate: the last row becomes [0.71, 0.71, 1.41].

props.caption: QKᵀ: each row is one token's scores

steps.title: Softmax each row
steps.body: Row by row, softmax turns scaled scores into weights that sum to 1. Token 1's row [0.71, 0, 0.71] becomes [0.40, 0.20, 0.40]; token 3's row becomes [0.25, 0.25, 0.50]. Without the sqrt(d_k) scaling, large dot products in high dimensions would push softmax towards one-hot weights with tiny gradients.

props.caption: Attention weights after scaling and softmax

steps.title: Blend the values
steps.body: Multiply the weights by V. With V = [[1, 0], [0, 2], [1, 1]], token 1's output is 0.40 x [1, 0] + 0.20 x [0, 2] + 0.40 x [1, 1] = [0.80, 0.80], and token 3's is [0.75, 1.0]. Every output row is a context-aware mix of all tokens' values, computed for all tokens in one matrix product.

steps.title: Many heads, then recombine
steps.body: With d_model = 512 and 8 heads, each head has its own 64-dimensional Q, K and V and its own attention pattern; one might track syntax, another nearby words. The 8 outputs of 64 are concatenated back to 512 and multiplied by W_O. Cost grows with seq_len², since every token scores every other.

nodes.label: 8 heads: Q, K, V (n x 64 each)

under_the_hood.takeaway: Self-attention is three matrix multiplications and a softmax: softmax(QKᵀ / sqrt(d_k)) V. Each token gets an output that mixes in every other token by learned relevance, all in parallel, at a cost that grows with the square of sequence length.
